newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Angry investors force Dhaka bourse shut.
newsitem.headline: Angry investors force Dhaka bourse shut.

text.p: Trading on the Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) was suspended on Monday as investors in the kerb market, angry over continuing slide in share prices, staged noisy agitation outside the bourse and forced its doors to shut.
Witnesses said brokers were scared off while agitators threatened tougher action.
"There was no trading. We could not get into the floor," broker Ahmed Iqbal Hasan, who is also the Vice-President of the DSE, told Reuters.
Hasan said he was not sure if trading would resume on Monday. "If the agitation continues, it will be difficult to resume trading," he said.

Thousans of traders in the kerb (unofficial) market, which operates outside the DSE building, also staged a sit-in to protest what they called was "deliberate pushing down of share prices by manipulators."
As hundreds of police guarded the shuttered entrance to the DSE, the protesters shouted demands for resignation of Finance Minister S.A.M.S. Kibria.
They accused the minister of failing to check the price fall and called for immediate government steps to revive investors' confidence.

The DSE all share price index closed 48.8 points down at 2,618.3 on a turnover of 6.4 million taka amid panic selling on Saturday, a working day on Moslem Bangladesh. The index was above 3,700 couple of weeks ago
The DSE officials said they had discussed the deadlock with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), the market watchdog, and the Ministry of Finance, and asked for remedies.
